Request URL string. This contains only the URL that is present in the actual
HTTP request. Take the following request:

```http
GET /status?name=ryan HTTP/1.1
Accept: text/plain
```

To parse the URL into its parts:

```js
new URL(`http://${process.env.HOST ?? 'localhost'}${request.url}`);
```

When `request.url` is `'/status?name=ryan'` and `process.env.HOST` is undefined:

```console
$ node
> new URL(`http://${process.env.HOST ?? 'localhost'}${request.url}`);
URL {
  href: 'http://localhost/status?name=ryan',
  origin: 'http://localhost',
  protocol: 'http:',
  username: '',
  password: '',
  host: 'localhost',
  hostname: 'localhost',
  port: '',
  pathname: '/status',
  search: '?name=ryan',
  searchParams: URLSearchParams { 'name' => 'ryan' },
  hash: ''
}
```

Ensure that you set `process.env.HOST` to the server's host name, or consider replacing this part entirely. If using `req.headers.host`, ensure proper
validation is used, as clients may specify a custom `Host` header.

Each address is a string in the form of `$IP:$PORT`.
If the connection was successful, then the last address is the one that the socket is currently connected to.

bufferSize.description:
This property shows the number of characters buffered for writing. The buffer
may contain strings whose length after encoding is not yet known. So this number
is only an approximation of the number of bytes in the buffer.

`net.Socket` has the property that `socket.write()` always works. This is to
help users get up and running quickly. The computer cannot always keep up
with the amount of data that is written to a socket. The network connection
simply might be too slow. Node.js will internally queue up the data written to a
socket and send it out over the wire when it is possible.

The consequence of this internal buffering is that memory may grow.
Users who experience large or growing `bufferSize` should attempt to
"throttle" the data flows in their program with `socket.pause()` and `socket.resume()`.

If `true`, `socket.connect(options[, connectListener])` was
called and has not yet finished. It will stay `true` until the socket becomes
connected, then it is set to `false` and the `'connect'` event is emitted. Note
that the `socket.connect(options[, connectListener])` callback is a listener for the `'connect'` event.

localFamily.description: The string representation of the local IP family. `'IPv4'` or `'IPv6'`.

remotePort.description:

Reference to the underlying socket. Usually, users will not want to access
this property.

After calling `outgoingMessage.end()`, this property will be nulled.

writable.description:
Is `true` if it is safe to call `writable.write()`, which means
the stream has not been destroyed, errored, or ended.

writableAborted.description: Returns whether the stream was destroyed or errored before emitting `'finish'`.

writableEnded.description:
Is `true` after `writable.end()` has been called. This property
does not indicate whether the data has been flushed, for this use `writable.writableFinished` instead.

writableFinished.description: Is set to `true` immediately before the `'finish'` event is emitted.

writableHighWaterMark.description: Return the value of `highWaterMark` passed when creating this `Writable`.

writableLength.description:
This property contains the number of bytes (or objects) in the queue
ready to be written. The value provides introspection data regarding
the status of the `highWaterMark`.

writableObjectMode.description: Getter for the property `objectMode` of a given `Writable` stream.

writableCorked.description:
Number of times `writable.uncork()` needs to be
called in order to fully uncork the stream.

errored.description: Returns error if the stream has been destroyed with an error.

writableNeedDrain.description: Is `true` if the stream's buffer has been full and stream will emit `'drain'`.

type.description: The resource type whose rows are filtered.

expiredIdentities.description: Identities past their scheduled deactivation that the worker disabled in this run.

expiredActivations.description: Ended role activations removed in this run.

expiredMemberships.description: Temporary group memberships past their end removed in this run.

expiredAssignments.description: Access-package assignments past their end removed in this run (their bindings and memberships expire on their own).

dryRun.description: Report what would change without writing anything.

limit.description: Most records examined per collection (a sample, for `selfCheck`); by default all of them.

resealed.description: Values re-sealed with the current secret (or, in a dry run, that would be), per collection.

unreadable.description: Values no configured secret opens, per collection: sealed with a secret that is gone.

current.description: Values already sealed with the current secret.

complete.description: Every record was examined; false when `limit` cut a collection short (the counts are a sample).

done.description:
Nothing sealed with a previous secret remains: the run examined everything and (in a dry run)
found nothing to re-seal. Only then can `previousSecrets` go.

cap.description: Most records counted per backlog check (default 1000); larger backlogs report the cap.

deliveryRetentionMs.description: The `deliveryRetentionMs` your sweep runs with (default 30 days), so its backlog is judged the same way.

graceMs.description: The `graceMs` your sweep runs with (default 5 minutes).

storage.description: The adapter's own view, when it can describe itself.

check.description: Stable identifier, for suppressing or alerting on one check.

count.description: How many records the finding concerns, when it is about stored data (capped at `cap`).

settings.description: Adapter settings worth checking in production (journal mode, durability, size, server version).

sent.description: Tenants whose owners were emailed, with the recipient count and the finding counts.

skipped.description: Tenants left alone: not active, digested within the interval, nothing to report, or no owner with an email.

sent.description: One entry per person emailed, with how many of their items end within the window.

skipped.description: Tenants left alone: not active, or with nothing new to remind anyone about.

now.description:
Epoch milliseconds to treat as now, for tests and backfills. By default each collection is
judged by the clock its writer uses: the authentication clock for sessions, devices,
relationships, the outbox, and audit hooks, and the wall clock for OAuth, SAML, and SSF records.

batchSize.description: Records read per transaction (default 500, 1-5000). Short transactions keep the write lock brief.

limit.description: The most records one run deletes (default 10000, at most 1000000); see `truncated`.

deliveryRetentionMs.description:
How long delivered and abandoned deliveries stay (outbox email, SMS, and webhook history, failed
Shared Signals deliveries): default 30 days, 0-3650 days. Pending deliveries are never swept.

graceMs.description: A margin past expiry before a record is deleted, against clock skew between instances (default 5 minutes, at most 1 day).

deleted.description: Records deleted per collection; collections with nothing to delete are omitted.

truncated.description: The run stopped at `limit` before finishing; more records may be due, so run it again.
